encounters.cc: Difficulty straightening fingers and progressive hand contracture

lines: Difficulty straightening fingers and progressive hand contracture
The patient presents with hand contractures following his Cardiology visit.
He reports that this problem has been gradually worsening over the past year.
He denies any trauma or previous similar issues.
His medical history is significant for type 2 diabetes mellitus and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD).
- Exploratory laparotomy with small bowel resection and primary anastomosis for perforated viscus
- Atorvastatin 40 mg PO daily at bedtime
- Insulin Glargine 20 units subcutaneous at bedtime
- Albuterol HFA inhaler 90 mcg (2 puffs) inhaled every 4-6 hours as needed for shortness of breath
Smoking: 45 pack-year history, currently smoking 1 pack per day.
Alcohol: Social use (1-2 drinks per month).
On physical examination, you notice puckering of the skin over the palmar surface of his hands and palpable fibrotic nodules along the course of the flexor tendons.
There is a flexion deformity at the metacarpophalangeal and proximal interphalangeal joints of the fourth and fifth fingers of both hands.
The patient is unable to fully extend these fingers.
No erythema, warmth, or tenderness is noted over the affected areas.
The rest of the musculoskeletal examination is unremarkable.

lines: Pain and tightness in lower legs with walking that improves with rest

The patient is started on a statin, antiplatelet therapy, and a supervised exercise program.

encounters.cc: Post-operative management following laparotomy for perforated bowel

lines: Post-operative management following laparotomy for perforated bowel
